author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: The supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, which locks our allocation window. I am not deploying the new model without a shadow run first. However, I will not accept any shadow deployment shipping without a formal sign off in place. This is a hard line. If the sign off is missing, the shadow run does not go live, and we stay on the current pipeline. I am not negotiating on this point because the legal duty to have reasonable stock available for advertised promotions means a silent failure here is a compliance breach, not just a missed forecast. We need the governance gate before we touch the live forecast path.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a non-negotiable line where the absence of a formal sign-off results in a refusal to deploy, regardless of other considerations.
